title: The Maryland Boy and the Exorcism That Inspired The Exorcist
excerpt: A 14-year-old boy in Maryland underwent an exorcism in 1949 after using a ouija board. The case, with no names in the press, inspired The Exorcist. What really happened?
content:
A 14-year-old boy from Maryland was allegedly subjected to an exorcism in 1949, according to accounts that the American press published without giving names. The topic comes from a Milenio 3 (Cadena SER) special on exorcisms, and on foro3d.com we review the real case behind The Exorcist. The story begins with an aunt fond of spiritualism who taught him to use the ouija board.

What was told and what is known today 👻

According to the accounts, after the aunt's death, noises and the movement of objects began in the house. The family first went to their Lutheran pastor and later to Catholic priests, and the boy, known as Roland Doe or Robbie Mannheim, was taken to St. Louis, where the priest William Bowdern led an exorcism for weeks at the Alexian Brothers hospital. William Peter Blatty drew inspiration from the case for his novel The Exorcist (1971), adapted into a film in 1973. Skeptics, such as Mark Opsasnick or Joe Nickell, maintain that much of it is based on rumors and that there is no credible evidence of a possession.

The ouija board that took the fame 🔮

The legend grew so much that even the ouija board seems to have come out ahead in the story: from a parlor game to the protagonist of a story that produced novels and films. It is worth separating what was told from what can be proven, and there the debate remains open. Do you know any detail about the case or the skeptical investigations? Tell us and share what you know.
